scenes.label: Roll out a SocTalk-based AI SOC in 20 minutes
scenes.narr: Rolling out a SocTalk-based AI SOC: an MSSP control plane and one tenant, on your own Proxmox host. Start to finish, about twenty minutes.

scenes.label: Before you start
items: A Proxmox host, KVM enabled, with 8 GB of RAM, 4 vCPU, and 60 GB of disk per VM
A Tailscale tailnet, and an API key with the keys:write scope
An SSH public key to authorize on every provisioned VM
A model API key for triage (any OpenAI-compatible provider)
scenes.narr: You need four things. A Proxmox host with room for the VMs. A Tailscale tailnet and an API key. An SSH key for the machines. And a model key for triage.

lines: $ launchpad init      # download + verify the plugins
scenes.narr: Install the launchpad binary from the GitHub releases. Let it verify its plugins, then start the console.

scenes.label: Open the console
scenes.narr: The console is a local web app. Point your browser at localhost, and you drive the whole rollout from three screens.

scenes.label: Network
scenes.narr: Every machine in the run joins one tailnet. Add the tailnet and its key here, then test that the key works before you rely on it.

scenes.label: Host
scenes.narr: The host is your Proxmox server. Choose the Proxmox platform, give it the API endpoint, and test the token before you rely on it.

scenes.label: The run form
scenes.narr: The run assigns the machines to that host and takes the admin login for the control plane. On screen, the secrets stay masked.

scenes.label: Launch
scenes.narr: Launch starts the rollout. It creates the machines, joins them to the tailnet, and installs the SOC stack on each.

scenes.label: Provisioning + install
scenes.narr: The install runs on its own, about fifteen minutes, mostly waiting on downloads. k3s and Helm, then the control plane and the tenant SOC stack. We fast forward past it.

scenes.label: On Proxmox
scenes.narr: On the Proxmox host, both machines are up: the MSSP control plane and the tenant, cloned from one template.

scenes.label: Tenant online
scenes.narr: In the console, the tenant comes online within a minute or two, running its own SOC stack.

scenes.label: Alerts flowing
scenes.narr: A built-in attack simulator runs techniques against the tenant endpoint. Each one arrives here as an investigation, newest first.

scenes.label: Cross-tenant dashboard
scenes.narr: This is the cross-tenant fleet view. Every investigation gets a first pass from the model, and what it cannot close on its own becomes a pending review for an analyst.

scenes.label: soctalk.ai
scenes.narr: Start your pilot at soctalk dot A I.
